newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico eyes dumping charges against U.S. beef.
newsitem.headline: Mexico eyes dumping charges against U.S. beef.

text.p: Mexico's National Association of Cattle Feeders (ANEG) is studying the possibility of presenting dumping charges against importers of U.S. beef, ANEG's director said Thursday.

"We are very worried about the current level of beef imports and are currently studying how to combat it (dumping) but we still do not know what strategy we are going to take," Enrique Lopez told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Lopez Lopez said the studies, also involving the National Livestock Confederation, were being carried out with the government and could end in countervaling duties, temporary tariffs or import quotas being slapped on U.S. beef.

Mexico has seen imports rise to current levels of 16,000 tonnes of beef per month from averages of 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes in 1995. Current levels are even higher than the 1994 records of up to 13,000 tonnes per month.
Current imports account for around 16 percent of national consumption. Lopez Lopez said net beef output in Mexico is around 105,000 tonnes per year, with up to 2,000 tonnes exported.

Lopez Lopez added that the association had tracked down beef imports of one cut called "La Bola" at prices of 18 pesos per kilo at the port of entry and 20 pesos per kilo in Mexico City. The same cut being sold in the United States at the price equivalent of 48 pesos per kilo, he said.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
